item.title: When, Where, and How Experience Becomes Structure: Mechanisms for Recursive Self-Improvement in LLM Agents
item.description: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) studies how AI systems modify themselves and carry those changes into the generation of subsequent improvements. LLM agents can pursue this process by using interaction experience to revise Prompt, Memory, Skill, and Harness in some cases while keeping the task-execution model’s weights fixed. item.title: Mind2Report: Expert-Level Commercial Report Synthesis via Cognitive Deep Research Agent
item.description: Synthesizing informative commercial reports from massive and noisy web sources is critical for high-stakes business decisions. Although recent deep research agents (DRAs) achieve notable progress, their reports remain limited in quality, reliability, and coverage. These mainly stem from ambiguous intents that cause search drift, retrieved web content that rapidly saturates the context window, and single-pass synthesis that limits report comprehensiveness. item.title: Persistent memory through triple-loop consolidation under stochastic unit turnover
item.description: Dissipative cognitive architectures maintain computation through continuous energy expenditure, where units that exhaust their energy are stochastically replaced with fresh random state. This creates a fundamental challenge: how can persistent, context-specific memory survive when all learnable state is periodically destroyed? item.title: Self-directed coaching: repositioning the client as the internalizing agent of developmental self-regulation a conceptual framework and research agenda for coaching theory and practice
item.description: Coaching has become one of the most widely deployed developmental interventions in organizational, educational, and health-professions settings, and the literature offers substantial evidence for its short-term benefits. Evidence on whether those benefits persist after formal coaching support is withdrawn is thinner and less systematic, and the question points to an unresolved tension at the field’s core. item.description: Abstract The proliferation of Generative Artificial Intelligence (Gen AI) powered by large language models (LLMs) has transformed the software development process, introducing new paradigms for code generation, debugging, testing, and maintenance. item.title: Post-Training on the Clock: Specializing a Small Language Model on a Consumer GPU
item.description: Abstract How should a language model be specialized for a target task when training is limited to one consumer GPU and a few hours? We study the allocation of a nominal three-hour training budget, with up to 0.3 additional hours, between supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO). item.description: In this paper, we study how targeted content injection can strategically disrupt social networks. Specifically, we address a practical limitation of the basic variant of the Friedkin–Johnsen (FJ) model, which prevents increasing the polarization and disagreement of the network, making it unable to reproduce real-world scenarios. item.title: MOSAIC: Unveiling the Moral, Social and Individual Dimensions of Large Language Models
item.description: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in sensitive applications including psychological support, healthcare, and high-stakes decision-making. item.title: Persona Conditioning as an Assessor-Sensitivity Probe for LLM-Based IR Evaluation
item.description: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used as relevance assessors in information retrieval (IR) evaluation, raising questions about how assessor framing affects judgment reliability and downstream system comparison. We study persona conditioning as a diagnostic mechanism for exposing LLM assessor sensitivity. item.title: MUSE: An Interactive Meta-Agent for Understanding and Steering LLM-powered Data Science Systems
item.description: Recent advances in large language models have enabled a new class of agentic data science systems that allow users to complete complex data science workflows through natural language. item.title: Viewpoints on inclusive education at the end of initial teacher preparation: Q methodology research
item.description: Abstract This study used Q methodology to explore the perspectives on inclusive education held by 44 student teachers completing their initial teacher education (ITE) programme at Qatar University. Participants ranked 44 statements along a quasi‐normal distribution; factor analysis yielded four distinct viewpoints. item.description: Background: Most Ebola virus disease research focuses on clinical diagnosis or static knowledge networks, limiting dynamic spatiotemporal analysis of epidemic evolution. item.description: Electrified agricultural machinery increasingly relies on permanent-magnet synchronous motor drives that must remain dependable under variable traction, terrain-induced vibration, thermal cycling, contamination, and intermittent duty. item.description: Recent research has established that generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is not a unitary workplace resource: exploratory and exploitative use orientations are associated with different forms of employee creativity, and their value depends on employees' capacity to integrate generated knowledge. item.title: From Coding to Creativity: Integrating Design Thinking into IT and Technology Education
item.description: This study examines how the integration of Design Thinking into Information Technology (IT) and technology education can bridge technical programming skills and creative, human-centered problem-solving.
